reasons: Reviewer recommends rejection: Facts match the cited sources after the corrections, including the attribution of the sequencing and executive-production credit to Questlove. The remaining issue is style: the German page mirrors the English structure sentence by sentence, which the style guide treats as a translation. Not rewritten here because the brief excludes style rewrites.

claims.claim: Born Lonnie Rashid Lynn Jr., 13 March 1972, Chicago, Illinois
claims.note: Both sources give date and place; artist page gives birth name.

claims.claim: Common is the first rapper with a Grammy, an Oscar and an Emmy; Recording Academy news item dated 14 September 2017
claims.note: Source confirms the first-rapper claim and the publication date September 14, 2017.

claims.claim: Fourth studio album as a major career high; Common calls the period one of the greatest times of his life
claims.note: Source: 'His fourth album Like Water For Chocolate'; 'one of the greatest times in my life.' German rendering is faithful.

claims.claim: Title from the film Like Water for Chocolate; people cooking and showing love; wanted something similar in music
claims.note: Source: 'people cooking food and showing their love'; 'showing it through the music'.

claims.claim: The Light was the first hit and the first song on mainstream radio
claims.note: Source: 'his first hit (The Light)'; 'the first song that I had on the radio, on mainstream radio.'

claims.claim: He knew it sounded good but never knew what it would become (quote translated)
claims.note: Source: 'I knew it sounded great but I never knew what it would get to be.' German is a faithful translation.

claims.claim: The Light listed under Best Rap Solo Performance in 2001
claims.note: Artist page lists 2001 Best Rap Solo Performance for The Light, with no label; wording now says listed, not nominated.

claims.claim: Femi Kuti is on the record; Common says getting him was incredible (unglaublich)
claims.note: Source: 'To get him on it was incredible.' Translation is faithful.

claims.claim: Geto Heaven was created for D'Angelo; D'Angelo wanted Chicken Grease and offered something in return
claims.note: Source: 'Geto Heaven was actually created for D'Angelo'; 'Can I get Chicken Grease and I'll give you something.'

claims.claim: Common says he got D'Angelo on Geto Heaven
claims.note: Source: 'I got him on Geto Heaven.'

claims.claim: Chicken Grease would have been Common's, in the lane of Cold Blooded, before it went to D'Angelo's Voodoo
claims.note: Source: 'would have been for me in the same lane as Cold Blooded'; 'the song on D'Angelo's Voodoo, Chicken Grease'.

claims.claim: Common says Questlove set the track order and truly executive-produced the album
claims.note: Source: 'Ahmir did the sequencing... he truly executive-produced that album.' Attribution corrected to Ahmir/Questlove as the subject.

claims.claim: Wendy Goldstein, his A&R, introduced him to his acting coach
claims.note: Source: 'My A&R Wendy Goldstein actually introduced me to my acting coach.'

claims.claim: Best Original Song at the 87th Academy Awards: Glory from Selma; credited to John Stephens (John Legend) and Lonnie Lynn (Common)
claims.note: Source: 'Glory' from Selma; Music and Lyric by John Stephens and Lonnie Lynn. Legend/Common names appear in the page caption.

claims.claim: Television Academy lists a 2015 Golden Globe win for Best Original Song
claims.note: Source: 'won the 2015 Golden Globe Award for Best Original Song' for Glory.

claims.claim: 2016 Grammys: Glory nominated for Best Rap Song and Best Rap/Sung Collaboration, won Best Song Written for Visual Media
claims.note: Artist page marks those labels as stated.

claims.claim: Common played civil rights leader James Bevel in Selma, a 2014 film
claims.note: Source: 'co-starred as Civil Rights Movement leader James Bevel' in Selma (2014).

claims.claim: 2017 Primetime Emmy for Outstanding Original Music and Lyrics for Letter to the Free, listed under the show 13th with Netflix as platform
claims.note: Source: Outstanding Original Music And Lyrics - 2017, show 13th, song Letter To The Free, platform Netflix.

claims.claim: Shared the Emmy with Robert Glasper and Karriem Riggins
claims.note: Source: 'shared the honor with GRAMMY-winner Robert Glasper and Karriem Riggins.'

claims.claim: One Emmy nomination, which was the win
claims.note: Page shows 1 nomination and 1 Emmy.

claims.claim: Emmy leaves him one Tony short of EGOT; club has 13 members so far
claims.note: Source: 'one Tony short of EGOT'; 'only 13 members so far.'

claims.claim: Best Rap Album nominations: 2006 Be, 2008 Finding Forever, 2010 Universal Mind Control, 2015 Nobody's Smiling, 2025 The Auditorium, Vol. 1
claims.note: All five entries appear under Best Rap Album with those years. Nominations are marked for 2010, 2015 and 2025; 2006 and 2008 carry no label.

claims.claim: Southside listed for 2008 in Best Rap Performance by a Duo or Group
claims.note: Entry present for 2008, unlabelled. Wording now says listed.

claims.claim: Three wins and 22 nominations in total
claims.note: Page totals: 3 wins and 22 nominations.

claims.claim: Television Academy bio lists the film titles, and Common narrated Bouncing Cats
claims.note: Film list matches. Page text: 'He also narrated the documentary Bouncing Cats' (verified on a second fetch).

claims.claim: Pete Rock and Common first worked together nearly 30 years before, on the 1996 diss track The Bitch In Yoo
claims.note: Source: 'Nearly 30 years since they first collaborated on Common's classic 1996 diss track The Bitch In Yoo.'

claims.claim: The Auditorium, Vol. 1 is both artists' first full-length release since 2021
claims.note: Source: 'first full-length offerings since 2021.'

claims.claim: Common has said a second volume is possible
claims.note: Source quotes Common to People: 'there may be a second volume.'

claims.claim: 2025 Best Rap Album nomination; When the Sun Shines Again nominated for Best Rap Performance
claims.note: Both entries are marked nominations in 2025.

claims.claim: Television Academy lists the 2003 Best R&B Song Grammy for Love of My Life and a Best Rap Performance by a Duo or Group Grammy for Southside, without a year
claims.note: Source: 'won the Grammy Award for Best R&B Song for ... Love of My Life'; 'second Grammy Award for Best Rap Performance by a Duo or Group for Southside'. No year.

claims.claim: Recording Academy artist page names Love of My Life as his first career Grammy
claims.note: Source biography: 'Common won his first career GRAMMY for Best R&B Song.'

claims.claim: Artist page lists Southside under 2008 without marking it as a win
claims.note: 2008 Southside entry is unlabelled.

claims.claim: FAQ: artist page gives three wins and 22 nominations, names Love of My Life (2003) as his first Grammy and marks Glory (2016) as a win
claims.note: Totals, first career Grammy and the Glory 2016 win all match the page.

claims.claim: Metadescription and summary: 2025 Grammy nomination for The Auditorium, Vol. 1; Oscar for Glory; Emmy for Letter to the Free; films American Gangster, Wanted, John Wick: Chapter 2
claims.note: All match the sources.
